newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit consolidates gains, but seen falling again.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit consolidates gains, but seen falling again.

text.p: The ringgit consolidated its overnight gains after being halted at 2.5220 resistance level, but the rise was not sustainable, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the ringgit would resume its downtrend against the dollar in the near term probably after Tuesday's U.S. presidential elections.
The ringgit recovered by nearly 100 points after hitting a seven-month low on Monday afternoon on profit-taking against a backdrop of a weaker dollar/yen, the dealers said.
"We doubt this sort of ringgit strength is sustainable," said research firm I.D.E.A. in its latest report.
It said Malaysian corporate players were still waiting for good levels to buy the dollar and much of offshore ringgit buying in the last two days was short-term play.
"General sentiment is still biased towards a stronger dollar/ringgit," I.D.E.A. said.
At 0845 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5215/25 a dollar against 2.5265/75 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday. It hit a seven-month low of 2.5330 a dollar on Monday.
Dealers said if the ringgit breached 2.5220 convincingly it would face a very strong resistance at 2.5180.
